verdict.rationale: SvelteKit's own docs say pages in src/routes are server-rendered so a user's first visit is as fast as possible, and that rendering modes can be mixed per page. A community report confirms clear server/client load separation. Nothing in the evidence documents streaming of server responses, so only the SSR half of the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: any documentation of streaming SSR or streamed data/promises, evidence of faster time-to-interactive via streaming, and independent hands-on corroboration of streaming.

support.subject: As a developer, I can render my application on the server with streaming support to reach interactivity faster

citations.quote: These will be server-rendered so that a user's first visit to your app is as fast as possible
SvelteKit allows for nicely mixing and matching different rendering types on different pages.
It is now very clear in what order items load and what loads on the server vs the client.
